insights.insight: Ad tech charges $5–$150 CPA on probabilistic signals inferred from behavior; each verified receipt here settles at ~$0.10 and confirms a purchase happened — no pixel, no lookback window, no model. That 50–200x cost delta is structural, not marginal.

Cookies are gone, device fingerprinting is degrading, and first-party data stops at your own ecosystem edge — none of these produce identity-free, cryptographically verified purchase signals across merchants. This protocol does.

133 unclassified receipts account for 35.8% of 14-day GMV at $271.65 average basket — six times the grocery average — meaning high-ticket and likely B2B transactions are flowing through but resisting standard merchant classification. Any targeting or measurement built on category data is working with a significant blind spot.

Simultaneous receipt activity is appearing in non-contiguous non-metro markets — MI, ME, AR, CA, IN, WI — with no geographic adjacency, following social graph topology rather than paid acquisition logic. Walmart leads 14-day brand volume at 79 receipts, consistent with this rural skew.

Amazon knows Amazon purchases; Walmart knows Walmart purchases; neither knows the other, and neither can sell that cross-ecosystem view to brands. A verified, identity-free signal that crosses merchant boundaries is the gap none of the incumbents can fill from inside their own walled garden.

insights.topic: Velocity divergence as a caution flag
insights.insight: Cumulative GMV has crossed $350K and receipt count is growing, but 7-day throughput has dropped from a $34,034 peak to $29,750 — rolling windows are contracting while cumulative totals grow. Brands evaluating this as a data source should track weekly run rate, not just cumulative figures.
